input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: no systematic GA-readiness assessment of Llama Stack has been done, TP feedback is scattered across support tickets, and the full inventory of gaps between current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar is not yet known. The epic produces the definitive GA scope — a gap inventory and remediation plan across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling — that determines the size and content of the downstream stability and hardening work.

## Scope

- Collect and consolidate Tech Preview feedback from support tickets and other feedback channels into a single triaged list.
- Assess the current published API surface against GA stability requirements (versioning state, deprecation posture, breaking changes across recent TP releases).
- Assess the upgrade story: what upgrade paths exist today between the last two TP releases, and what testing has been done.
- Assess scale limits: documented or observed limits of the current distribution under GA-representative workloads.
- Assess error handling quality across the API surface and operator.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: a prioritized gap inventory with remediation estimates, explicitly identifying which gaps are GA-blocking and which are not.
- Flag any gap whose remediation would change the approach or structure of the stability and hardening work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single GA-readiness assessment document exists that inventories gaps in all four enumerated areas: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Every gap entry states the current TP behavior, the GA bar it fails to meet, and a remediation estimate.
- TP feedback from support tickets is consolidated and each item is either mapped to a gap entry or explicitly ruled out of GA scope with a reason.
- The document identifies which gaps are GA-blocking, producing a definitive GA scope that the stability and hardening work can be planned against.
- Gaps whose remediation would require a different approach than API versioning and hardening (e.g., architectural rework) are explicitly called out.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. This epic is the direct delivery of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and GA hardening

## Description

This epic delivers the API stability guarantee that GA requires for Llama Stack: versioned APIs, a published deprecation policy, a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases, and remediation of the quality gaps (error handling, scale limits) identified by the GA-readiness assessment. It converts the Tech Preview component into one whose published API surface carries a stability commitment.

## Gating Dependency

This epic's scope is gated by the GA-readiness assessment: until the assessment lands, the size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate. The assessment's gap inventory rewrites this epic's remediation scope; the versioned-API, deprecation-policy, and upgrade-path deliverables are fixed by the strategy and proceed once the assessment defines the hardening scope around them.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning for the published API surface of the Llama Stack distribution.
- Define and publish a deprecation policy for the published API surface.
- Implement and test an upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases, including migration of existing LlamaStackDistribution custom resources.
- Remediate GA-blocking gaps in error handling across the API surface and operator, as identified by the GA-readiness assessment.
- Remediate GA-blocking scale-limit gaps as identified by the GA-readiness assessment, including documenting validated limits.
- Address every gap the GA-readiness assessment marks GA-blocking within this component's surfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning scheme is applied consistently across the surface.
- A deprecation policy is published covering the versioned API surface.
- An upgrade from each of the last two Tech Preview releases to the GA candidate is tested and passes, including custom-resource migration, with the procedure documented as part of the upgrade deliverable.
- Every gap the GA-readiness assessment marked GA-blocking and assigned to this component's surfaces has a merged remediation or an explicit, reviewed waiver recorded with a reason.
- Error-handling behavior on the published API surface returns structured, documented errors for failure cases identified in the assessment.
- Scale limits validated during remediation are recorded and handed to the support-posture work for inclusion in the supported configuration matrix.
- Rollback/compatibility: consumers of the existing TP API surface are not broken without a deprecation-policy-compliant path (the strategy replaces TP behavior with GA guarantees).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. This epic delivers HLR-2 in full, plus the assessment-driven hardening scope produced under HLR-1.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place that GA requires for Llama Stack: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. It is a distinct work product from the code stability work — policy and support-engineering deliverables with their own review cycle through product and support organizations.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution (availability and operational targets appropriate to a supported platform component).
- Define and document the backport policy: which release lines receive fixes, for how long, and how security and critical fixes are delivered.
- Define and validate the supported configuration matrix: the combinations of providers, versions, and deployment configurations that are supported at GA.
- Align the supported configuration matrix with validated scale limits handed over from the API stability and hardening work, and with the GA scope defined by the readiness assessment.
- Publish these artifacts through the support and product channels used for GA platform components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and published for the GA distribution.
- A backport policy is documented and published, covering release lines, fix eligibility, and security-fix handling.
- A supported configuration matrix is documented and published, enumerating supported provider, version, and deployment combinations.
- The configuration matrix incorporates the validated scale limits handed over from the stability and hardening work where applicable.
- The support-posture artifacts are reviewed and accepted by the owning product and support organizations.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. This epic delivers HLR-3 in full.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack integration

## Description

This epic makes the safety-guardrails integration via TrustyAI a supported, documented integration for GA Llama Stack distributions, promoted from an experimental flag. The TrustyAI team owns the integration deliverable; where changes on the Llama Stack distribution side are needed to complete the integration, they are coordinated with the Llama Stack owning team within this epic's scope.

## Scope

- Promote the TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack distributions from experimental-flag status to supported status.
- Validate the integration against GA-bar quality criteria: functional coverage of the guardrails surface, failure behavior, and configuration paths that supported customers will use.
- Document the integration: supported configuration, capabilities, and limitations, suitable for inclusion in GA product documentation.
- Define and record the support posture for the integration (how issues are triaged between the TrustyAI and Llama Stack support surfaces).
- Remove or graduate the experimental flag so the integration is available as a supported path in GA distributions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guardrails integration is enabled through a supported (non-experimental) configuration path in GA Llama Stack distributions.
- The integration passes a validation pass over three concrete surfaces — functional coverage of the guardrails capabilities exposed through the integration, failure behavior (how guardrails requests degrade and report when TrustyAI services are unavailable or misconfigured), and the supported configuration paths — with failures either fixed or documented as explicit limitations.
- Documentation of the integration (setup, capabilities, limitations) is complete and technically reviewed against the implemented behavior.
- The support/triage path for integration issues is defined and agreed between the TrustyAI and Llama Stack teams.
- No experimental or TP label remains on the integration in GA distribution artifacts or documentation.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. This epic delivers HLR-4 in full.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default

## Description

This epic enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate that users currently must pass to see Llama Stack management surfaces.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management enablement from an opt-in (Tech Preview gate) to default-on for entitled clusters.
- Preserve entitlement gating: the Llama Stack management surfaces appear by default only on clusters with the required entitlement.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in flow (flag, banner, acknowledgement, or equivalent gate) for Llama Stack management.
- Verify the Llama Stack management surfaces (navigation, resource lists, and status views served by the Dashboard) render and function correctly in the default-on state.
- Update Dashboard feature-flag defaults and any accompanying configuration documentation for the default-on behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with a Llama Stack distribution present, the Dashboard shows Llama Stack management surfaces with no opt-in action required by the user.
- On a cluster without the required entitlement, the Llama Stack management surfaces remain hidden.
- The Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management no longer appears in the Dashboard.
- The default-on state passes the Dashboard's existing feature-integration test coverage for the Llama Stack management surfaces.
- Feature-flag defaults and configuration documentation reflect the default-on behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). This epic delivers HLR-5 in full.

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift and TP migration notes

## Description

This epic uplifts the Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes for users moving from Tech Preview releases to GA. It runs last so the documentation describes what was actually built: the API stability guarantees, the support posture, the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration, and the Dashboard default-enablement behavior.

## Scope

- Content outline:
  - GA overview and support statements for Llama Stack (maturity, supported configuration matrix, SLO targets, backport policy as delivered by the support-posture work).
  - API stability documentation: versioning scheme and deprecation policy as delivered by the stability work.
  - Migration guide from Tech Preview releases, including the tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases and custom-resource migration steps.
  - TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation for GA distributions (setup, capabilities, limitations).
  - Dashboard default-enablement behavior for entitled clusters.
  - Removal or update of all Tech Preview caveats, experimental labels, and opt-in instructions across Llama Stack documentation topics.
- Author all topics to Red Hat GA documentation standards and migrate them through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers every topic in the content outline above, at GA standard.
- A migration guide exists that walks a TP user through upgrading to GA, consistent with the tested upgrade path delivered by the stability work.
- No Llama Stack documentation topic retains Tech Preview or experimental labeling for GA-supported behavior.
- All content is technically reviewed against the implemented GA behavior (the delivered API stability, support posture, guardrails integration, and Dashboard enablement), and review findings are resolved.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-6 (P2)**: Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. This epic delivers HLR-6 in full.
